statement.text:
An undirected graph is called a locally finite Cayley graph of a group G if
its vertex set can be identified with the set of elements of G in such a way that, for
some finite generating set X = X −1 of G not containing 1, two vertices g and h are
adjacent if and only if g −1 h ∈ X. Do there exist two finitely generated groups with
the same locally finite Cayley graph, one of which is periodic and the other is not
periodic?                                                               V. I. Trofimov
